claims.text: VKA + hemodynamic instability: ACG/ESGE strongly recommend PCC (rapid onset).
claims.quote: For patients with hemodynamic instability on vitamin K antagonists (VKA), the ACG and ESGE strongly recommend infusing prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC) due to rapid onset of action.

claims.text: PCC label: give vit K concurrently.
claims.quote: Administer Vitamin K concurrently to patients receiving BALFAXAR.

claims.text: Life-threatening bleed + DOAC w.in 24 h: PCC can be considered.
claims.quote: Alternatively, PCC can be considered in patients with life-threatening bleeding who had taken a DOAC within the past 24 hours of presentation.

claims.text: Dabigatran: idarucizumab (Praxbind) when reversal is needed.
claims.quote: PRAXBIND is indicated in patients treated with Pradaxa when reversal of the anticoagulant effects of dabigatran is needed

claims.text: Andexanet (Andexxa) ⍉sold in the US after Dec 22, 2025.
claims.quote: Andexxa will no longer be manufactured for or sold in the U.S. by AstraZeneca after December 22, 2025.

claims.text: ACG: ⍉routine vit K in acute GI bleeding (slow onset).
claims.quote: The ACG does not advise routine use of Vitamin K in acute GI bleeding due to its relatively slow onset of action with effect seen around 24 hours and subsequent delays in reaching a therapeutic target once the vitamin K antagonist is restarted.
